title: extcap: sshdump: Terminate remote command if no packets captured
description:
Dumpcap and tcpdump, when reading from a network interface and using a
capture filter that excludes all incoming packets, may sit indefinitely
without reading from stdin or writing to stdout or stderr. They will
close if they receive a SIGHUP or other signals.

However, when a remote SSH command is executed directly without a PTY,
the connection ends by default without a SIGHUP. OTOH, using a PTY is
a problem because stdout and stderr would be mixed, and the binary data
would be transformed (e.g., newlines to CRLF, which at least is obvious
and fails capture immediately as it disturbs the pcapng SHB block type).

The SSH protocol does have support for sending signals over a channel[1],
and libssh supports that, and OpenSSH's server has supported it since 7.9
(October 2018)[2]. So we should send HUP when closing. In order to do
that, we need to have a graceful shutdown callback that will break out
of the loop. If there is no data incoming, using a blocking read in the
loop is a problem. libssh provides ssh_select to use instead, so use
that.

On non Win32, we can set up a self-pipe, monitor it along with the
libssh fd, and exit cleanly. This doesn't work on Win32 for multiple
reasons - Windows can't select() on pipes, and what libssh provides
is a wrapper around select(). We could setup a socketpair, using a
loopback socket or (on recent Windows) a AF_UNIX socket, although again
Windows doesn't provide socketpair() so we'd have to implement that.
We'd also need to set up sshdump to read the control in pipe, since the
current signaling method doesn't work on Windows (#17131).

Ping #14239. This still needs a non Win32 solution. Also the same
solution should be used for wifidump and sshdig (but not apparently
ciscodump), so perhaps the loop should go into ssh-base.

[1] - https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4254#section-6.9
[2] - https://www.openssh.org/txt/release-7.9

changes_data.diff:
@@ -121,6 +121,39 @@ ssh_session create_ssh_connection(const ssh_params_t* ssh_params, char** err_inf
  */
 int ssh_channel_printf(ssh_channel channel, const char* fmt, ...);
 
+/**
+ * @brief Sets up ssh_async_loop_read to allow graceful shutdown
+ *
+ * Creates a self-pipe (eventually, on Windows, a SOCKET, but not
+ * implemented yet) that allows ssh_async_loop_read to be interrupted
+ * when a graceful shutdown is signaled for by the main application.
+ * This is useful for, among other things, when SSH has EXEC'd a command
+ * like dumpcap and tcpdump that might sit without attempting to read
+ * from stdin or write to stdout or stderr indefinitely if, e.g., a
+ * capture filter was given that excludes all packets, and thus will
+ * not exit unless a SIGHUP is manually issued, such as by ssh_cleanup.
+ *
+ * @param extcap_conf Pointer to the extcap parameters structure.
+ */
+bool ssh_base_setup_graceful_shutdown(extcap_parameters *extcap_conf);
+
+/**
+ * @brief Asynchronously reads the output of a single SSH command
+ *
+ * Loops to read the output of a single SSH command and write it to an open
+ * FILE pointer. Calls ssh_select to wait on the channel and optionally the
+ * graceful shutdown indication, if ssh_base_setup_graceful_shutdown was
+ * called (non-Windows only). If the SSH channel's stdout reaches EOF, the
+ * function then reads the channel's stderr and writes that to the current
+ * process's stderr.
+ *
+ * @param sshs The SSH session
+ * @param channel The SSH channel to read
+ * @param fp The FILE to write the channel's stdout to
+ * @return EXIT_SUCCESS if successful, EXIT_FAILURE otherwise.
+ */
+int ssh_async_loop_read(ssh_session sshs, ssh_channel channel, FILE* fp);
+
 /* Clean the current ssh session and channel. */
 
 /**
